events.content: custom AI silicon market share 2025 Google TPU AWS Trainium NVIDIA AMD

**Bottom line:** Google and Amazon do not disclose standalone TPU or Trainium revenue, respectively, so there is no company-reported, auditable market-share figure for either accelerator in 2025 or 2026. Amazon’s disclosed figure combines Trainium with Graviton—more than a $10 billion annual revenue run rate at Q4 2025—rather than separating Trainium. [[1]]

| Market-share measure | 2025 | 2026 estimate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Google TPU | Not disclosed / no robust independent 2025 figure found | ~6–8% of data-center AI-accelerator revenue or deployed-FLOPS-based market, depending on the methodology used. [[2]]|
| AWS Trainium / Inferentia | Not disclosed / no robust independent 2025 figure found | ~2–3% in one 2026 estimate; a separate August 2026 analyst-based estimate puts the combined Trainium/Inferentia share near 5%. [[2]] [[3]]|

The appropriate 2026 takeaway is therefore **TPU roughly 6–8% and Trainium/Inferentia roughly 2–5%**, but these are third-party estimates rather than reported results and should not be treated as precise, directly comparable revenue shares. [[2]] [[3]]

**What supports the direction of share gains:** AWS stated that Trainium2 was fully subscribed, with **1.4 million chips landed** by its Q4 2025 results, and that it powered most Bedrock inference; this demonstrates rapid adoption but does not establish Trainium-only revenue or market share. [[4]] [[1]] Google’s TPU scale was also reinforced by Anthropic’s commitment for access to up to **one million TPUs**, with capacity coming online through 2026, although that is a capacity commitment rather than TPU revenue recognized by Google. [[3]]

**Market context:** ASIC-based AI-server shipments are projected to reach **27.8%** of the server market in 2026, with custom-ASIC shipments forecast to grow **44.6% year over year**, versus **16.1%** for merchant GPUs; that expansion is the structural reason TPU and Trainium can gain share even while Nvidia remains dominant. [[5]] Estimates still place Nvidia at roughly **73–80%** of AI-accelerator revenue in mid-2026, so TPU and Trainium remain meaningful but distinctly secondary platforms in the overall market. [[3]]
